chapter_title.en: Chapter 100 – The smallness of the number of the Momineen

gradings: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (9/290)

translations.en: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Al-Nadr, from Yahya ibn Abi Khalid Al-Qammat, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! How few we are — if we were to gather together upon a sheep, we would not (even be able to) finish it.' So he said: 'Shall I narrate to you something more strange than that? The Emigrants and the Helpers were gone,' — and he gestured with his hand — 'except three.'

Humran said: 'So I said: "May I be sacrificed for you! What is the state of Ammar?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on Ammar — Abu al-Yaqzan — he pledged allegiance and was killed as a martyr." So I said within myself: "What thing is more superior than martyrdom?" So he looked at me and said: "Perhaps you think he is like the three. Far be it! Far be it!"

en.أَبَا الْيَقْظَانِ: Abu al-Yaqzan ('the Alert/Wakeful') — the kunya (agnomen) of Ammar ibn Yasir
en.أَيْهَاتَ: far be it — an expression of emphatic negation and impossibility, denying any equivalence
en.الثَّلَاثَةِ: the three — Salman al-Farsi, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who alone among the Emigrants and Helpers maintained unwavering allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)
en.الْأَنْصَارُ: the Helpers — the people of Medina who aided the Prophet (SAWW) and the Emigrants
en.الْمُهَاجِرُونَ: the Emigrants — the companions who migrated with the Prophet (SAWW) from Mecca to Medina
en.بَايَعَ: pledged allegiance — gave bay'ah, here referring to Ammar's pledge after the passing of the Prophet (SAWW)
en.شَهِيداً: as a martyr — one who is killed in the path of God, a rank of high honour

seo_questions.en: What did Imam al-Baqir (AS) say about the rank of Ammar ibn Yasir compared to Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad?

summaries.en: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) responds to Humran ibn A'yan's remark about the small number of true believers by pointing to a still more astonishing reality: nearly all the Emigrants and Helpers abandoned the true path after the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), save for only three — Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad. When Humran asks about Ammar ibn Yasir's standing, the Imam affirms Ammar's martyrdom with supplication for his mercy, yet — perceiving Humran's unspoken assumption — emphatically declares that Ammar's rank is not equivalent to those three steadfast companions, underscoring the supreme spiritual station of unwavering allegiance.

text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا أَقَلَّنَا لَوِ اجْتَمَعْنَا عَلَى شَاةٍ مَا أَفْنَيْنَاهَا فَقَالَ أَ لَا أُحَدِّثُكَ بِأَعْجَبَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمُهَاجِرُونَ وَ الْأَنْصَارُ ذَهَبُوا إِلَّا وَ أَشَارَ بِيَدِهِ ثَلَاثَةً

قَالَ حُمْرَانُ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا حَالُ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ عَمَّاراً أَبَا الْيَقْظَانِ بَايَعَ وَ قُتِلَ شَهِيداً فَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي مَا شَيْ‏ءٌ أَفْضَلَ مِنَ الشَّهَادَةِ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيَّ فَقَالَ لَعَلَّكَ تَرَى أَنَّهُ مِثْلُ الثَّلَاثَةِ أَيْهَاتَ أَيْهَاتَ .

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Al Nazar, from Yahya Bin Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran Bin Ayn who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! How few we are. If we were to gather together upon a sheep (feast), we would not (be able to) finish it’. So heasws said: ‘Shall Iasws narrate to you with something more strange than that? The Emigrants and the Helpers were gone (at the time of Amir Al-Momineenasws) except for’, and heasws gestured with hisasws hand, ‘three’ (Salmanas, Abu Zarras and Miqdadas)’.

Humran (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is the state of Ammar?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on Ammar, the alert. He pledged allegiance (to Abu Bakr) and was killed as a martyr’. So I said within myself, ‘What thing is more superior than the martyrdom?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> looked at me and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Perhaps you view that he is like the (other) three. Far be it! Far be it!’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Uramah from al-Nadr from Yahya ibn abu Khalid al-Qammat from Humran ibn ‘Ayun who has said the following: “Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, how small is our number! It is so small that all combined feasting on a goat cannot finish it.’ The Imam asked, ‘Do you want to hear more astonishing things? The immigrants (Muslim of Makkah) and supporters (Muslim of Madina) all went (to abu Bakr).’ He (the Imam) pointed with his hands, ‘except three, (Salman, abu Dhar and Miqdad) who remained as true supporters of Amir al- Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib, recipient of divine supreme covenant).’ I (Humran) then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what about ‘Ammar?’ The Imam said, ‘May Allah grant him favors, the alert man pledged allegiance (to abu Bakr) but he died as a martyr.’ I (Humran) then said to myself that there is nothing better than martyrdom. The Imam looked at me and said, ‘Perhaps you thought he was like one of the three. That is far remote from reality.’”
